question: In 1884, shipwrecked sailors killed and ate the cabin boy to survive. Why does Sandel retell the case?
answer: To test utilitarian thinking. The crew of the Mignonette, adrift for weeks, killed the sick 17-year-old Richard Parker, and three men lived. A court convicted two of murder. Sandel asks whether saving three lives justified taking one, or whether some acts are wrong whatever their benefits, as many people feel.
move: Test a principle on a hard case before trusting it on easy ones.
simply: Starving sailors killed the weakest boy so the rest could live. Was it right to save three by killing one? Most people feel it wasn't.
why: Hard cases show what we really believe. Asking 'would I accept this rule in the worst case?' is a quick test for any moral or policy argument.

book.title: Justice
book.author: Michael J. Sandel
